newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil April trade gap reaches $477 mln - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Brazil April trade gap reaches $477 mln - ministry.

text.p: Brazil posted a trade deficit of $213 million in the third week of April, taking the deficit for the month so far to $477 million, a spokeswoman for the Industry and Commerce Ministry said.
Imports in April's third week were $1.314 billion, while exports were $1.101 billion, the spokeswoman said.
Brazil posted trade deficits of $170 million in April's first week and $94 million in the second week.
In the third week, exports averaged $220.2 million a day, compared with $202.1 million in the first week and $220.6 million in the second week, the spokeswoman said.
Imports in the third week averaged $262.8 million a day, up from $244.5 million in the first week and $239.4 million in the second week, she said.
For the month so far, exports averaged $215.1 million a day while imports averaged $249.2 million.
When added to a $3.06 billion trade deficit posted by Brazil in the first three months of the year, April's figures take the trade gap in the year so far to $3.537 billion.
